I'm curious how it all works. In my brain I'm just assuming USB is a catch-all for a handful of ports, including the video ports, but that can't be right. 

I did notice though that Idle Skilling lagged a lot less in Realm (not that it helps once the damage numbers stack up enough), and it feels like other games have been smoother as well. 

Really curious what the hell goes on in that tower of mine sometimes, too stupid to figure it out.

🤔  If I had to hazard a guess as to what's going on, I'd bet there's some kind of periodic check that's being ran in-game in the main process/thread that ends up checking for the presence of a controller or other related device, which ends up checking what's plugged into each and every USB input device/port.

However, when that power setting is enabled, it ends up taking a long amount of time because the way it's checking each device ends up needing to "wake" it/restore power first, which is probably very costly in terms of time. 🐌  And since the check is being ran from the primary thread of the application, everything gets stuck waiting for the now time-consuming check to complete before it can continue operating as normal, such as updating what's happening on-screen etc. 🛑 

But when that setting is disabled, each of those devices is already "awake" or powered on, meaning it doesn't have to wait on Windows powering it up before it can do whatever check it's trying to do. It runs through the checks lightning fast, never getting to the point where it's holding up the game from doing what it's wanting to do. 🏎️ 

Of course this is 100% speculation, and I have no actual idea of what's going on. If that *is* what's happening, the ultimate solution would be making a change in the code that's performing these checks to go about it in a more performant way.
